parse.desc: parse_int_header then mystrtou32_modulo; base 16 after &h or 0x, else base 10; value reduced modulo 2**32; 0 when no digit is read
GetInt: optional &h or 0x selects %x, else %d; swscanf into int; throws on no match

post.desc: stored value is the visible value
percent value, divided by 100 at or before use
1 becomes 0 and 3 becomes 1; every other value becomes 0

stylefield.name: name
stylefield.note: Both renderers strip leading '*' characters. The stored name is not equivalent. libass keeps the bytes and replaces only an empty name with "Default" (ass.c:744-747). xy replaces an empty name with "Default" and maps the name "default" to "Default" without regard to case (STS.cpp:2263,1479). VSFilterMod also replaces an empty name through AddStyle. Name resolution therefore differs for mixed-case and empty names. The matrix records the conversion; it does not resolve the lookup.

stylefield.name: fontname
stylefield.note: Every renderer keeps the name text. VSFilterMod passes the name through WToT (STS.cpp:1862, TextFile.cpp:567-573). The pinned VSFilterMod project sets CharacterSet Unicode (subtitles.vcxproj:35), so WToT is the identity for that build and no character changes. A narrow-character build would truncate each wide character. The build scope is unknown by default.

stylefield.name: primarycolour
stylefield.note: assx checks only that the value has a valid digit in its selected base (hex after &H or 0x, else decimal). The ASS convention writes a colour as &HAABBGGRR& hex. assx does not check cross-renderer equivalence of the stored form. libass byte-swaps at parse (parse_color_header, ass.c:338-342) and reads channels with the _r/_g/_b/_a macros (ass_parse.h:26-29). xy stores the integer as a COLORREF and reverses red and blue at use (RTS.cpp:59-62,1278-1328). The byte order was not followed to the drawn pixel, and that check is out of scope by decision.

stylefield.name: secondarycolour
stylefield.note: Same valid-value rule as primarycolour. Byte-order equivalence is out of scope.

stylefield.name: outlinecolour
stylefield.note: libass reads the SSA TertiaryColour name here (ass.c:694). In SSA, libass then overwrites OutlineColour from BackColour (ass.c:696-697). The v4+ path does not. Byte-order equivalence is out of scope.

stylefield.name: backcolour
stylefield.note: Same valid-value rule as primarycolour. Byte-order equivalence is out of scope.

stylefield.name: bold
stylefield.note: Every renderer applies !! to the integer, so any nonzero value becomes 1. Garbage input differs: libass yields 0 (ass.c:299) while GetInt throws (STS.cpp:1249). ASS022 already reports the malformed case.

stylefield.name: italic
stylefield.note: Same boolean rule as bold.

stylefield.name: underline
stylefield.note: Same boolean rule as bold. xy and VSFilterMod read this field only for sver 5 and later.

stylefield.name: strikeout
stylefield.note: Same boolean rule as bold. xy and VSFilterMod read this field only for sver 5 and later.

stylefield.name: fontsize
stylefield.note: libass stores a double. xy and VSFilterMod store a 32-bit float. A value with more than seven significant digits can round differently. ASS012 reports that case. The conversion is value-dependent, so the comparison resolves per value.

stylefield.name: scalex
stylefield.note: libass divides by 100 at parse. xy and VSFilterMod store percent and divide by 100 at use (RTS.cpp:430-431,736). All three clamp negatives to 0. The ratio is equivalent for a value that survives the float32 step.

stylefield.name: scaley
stylefield.note: Same rule as scalex.

stylefield.name: spacing
stylefield.note: Ignored by decision. assx does not check this field. The negative clamp is build-conditional in VSFilterMod. The clamp sits inside #ifndef _VSMOD (patch f002, STS.cpp:1899-1901), so a _VSMOD build keeps a negative spacing. A mod-build-version question cannot be resolved from the pinned source alone, so this field stays unmodeled for VSFilterMod.

stylefield.name: angle
stylefield.note: Same double versus float32 question as fontsize. No clamp in either renderer.

stylefield.name: outline
stylefield.note: All three clamp negatives to 0. Same float32 precision question as fontsize.

stylefield.name: shadow
stylefield.note: All three clamp negatives to 0. Same float32 precision question as fontsize.

stylefield.name: borderstyle
stylefield.note:
Policy: assx has no BorderStyle accepted-set check. ASS011 can still report a fractional integer field. ASS033 reports the verified box-scaling condition; ASS034 reports the value-4 mode difference. Neither rule supplies edits. Both require matching resolved ASS v4+ fields and complete rows. BorderStyle must be a whole decimal integer. ASS033 also requires positive ScaleX, ScaleY, and Outline, with at least one scale different from 100. Those numbers must have equal float32 and float64 values. Its target pair must include Mod and either traditional renderer. ASS034 requires libass and either VSFilter renderer. The rules describe Style definitions, including unused Styles. They do not trace Dialogue overrides or prove final pixels. Malformed, hexadecimal, SSA, and v4++ inputs remain outside these checks. Status: source-verified for all three pinned renderers. Matching mode selection does not prove equal pixels.
Conversion: libass keeps the integer from the Style row (ass.c:709). ass_reset_render_context copies it into border_style (ass_render.c:1097). xy maps file value 3 to internal value 1. File value 1 and every other integer become internal value 0 (STS.cpp:1540). VSFilterMod uses the same conversion (STS.cpp:1903). Internal 0 means outline; internal 1 means box. File value 0 does not disable the outline. File values 2, 5, 6, and -1 also select the outline path in all three sources. libass tests exact values 3 and 4; other integers use its normal border path (ass_render.c:1419-1467,2467-2487,3009-3010).
Value 1: all three select a glyph outline and an offset shadow. Outline controls border width. OutlineColour supplies the border colour. BackColour supplies the shadow colour. Zero width can remove the outline; the BorderStyle value alone does not promise a visible border.
Value 3: libass builds rectangles from glyph advance, spacing, ascent, and descent. It combines these rectangles within bitmap runs (ass_render.c:1419-1458,2643-2720). This is not one rectangle for the whole event. The box uses OutlineColour; its offset shadow uses BackColour (ass_render.c:827-848). xy creates a rectangle for each CWord from width, ascent, and descent. It copies outline colour and alpha into the polygon (RTS.cpp:561-578). PaintOutline and PaintShadow select that polygon (xy_overlay_paint_machine.cpp:116-134). VSFilterMod creates the same kind of CWord polygon (RTS.cpp:662-685). Its outline and shadow passes draw the polygon with separate colour slots (RTS.cpp:1347-1397,1427-1468). Word boundaries, Style changes, and line breaks can therefore affect boxes. The term opaque box does not mean forced opacity; colour alpha still applies.
Value 3 limits: libass clamps each computed box padding component to at least 64 internal units. It explicitly repeats font scaling to emulate VSFilter (ass_render.c:1433-1451). xy keeps font scaling on the box polygon (RTS.cpp:428-431,561-577). VSFilterMod marks the polygon isOpaqueBox and uses scale 1 in Transform (RTS.cpp:286-287,683). Thus non-100 font scales need separate checks. With Outline=0, the unshifted box is not drawn. A nonzero Shadow can still draw a shifted box. With both values zero, only text remains. libass selects box flags from border and shadow widths (ass_render.c:1419-1421,2467-2487,2732-2740). xy gates the box outline on rounded scaled widths (RTS.cpp:1259-1261). VSFilterMod tests the width sum before drawing it (RTS.cpp:1427). Fractional widths can select different passes. These paths do not establish equal geometry or blending.
Value 4: libass retains the normal glyph outline. render_text skips normal shadow images (ass_render.c:829). After text rendering, add_background adds one axis-aligned rectangle for the complete event bounds, including all lines (ass_render.c:2759-2790,2994-3010). It uses final BackColour and fade. Positive final shadow_x and shadow_y expand both sides of the bounds; negative values add no padding. Outline contributes to the event bounds. The rectangle is limited to the frame. It is added after glyph clipping, so a vector clip does not cut its mask (ass_render.c:881,2781-2788). xy and VSFilterMod convert file value 4 to outline mode. They do not reach a whole-event background path from this Style value.
Resets: named and bare r restore BorderStyle with the other Style values. libass copies BorderStyle in ass_reset_render_context (ass_render.c:1097). xy and VSFilterMod replace the word Style (RTS.cpp:2643-2647,3589-3593). libass chooses the whole-event background from final border_style, while individual glyphs retain their own border_style (ass_render.c:2138,3009). A reset between modes 3 and 4 therefore needs its own rendering check.
Build scope: the VSFilterMod loader mapping has no _VSMOD guard. Its box transform scale exception also has no guard. _VSMOD changes colour, blending, spacing, and clipping paths. _LUA can change box transforms (RTS.cpp:124-169,1332-1468). The pinned subtitles project defines both symbols (subtitles.vcxproj:95,113,132,145). The base mode comparison assumes no extension tags or Lua handlers. No VSFilter binary was run here.
Runtime check: the existing Windows amd64 libass DLL reported the pinned commit f61db567e6593df3470e91594bcd4ad2d0473aff. Its SHA-256 was e605e7f73e84c734f06d5c529948998824b2f330c8450fecb946d27c3519e72d. The Meson build used release and shared-library settings. Runtime logs reported FriBidi 1.0.16 and HarfBuzz-ng 14.2.1. The existing rendercheck helper compared exact RGBA frames at 640x360 and 25 fps. Fonts came only from the pinned libass compare/test directory, with ASS_FONTPROVIDER_NONE. The fixture used Aileron 32, two unequal text lines, ScaleX=ScaleY=100, Alignment=2, Outline=3, and Shadow=4. OutlineColour was opaque red; BackColour was half-transparent green. The event ran from 0 to 200 ms. Each comparison sampled 12 frames, including timing boundaries. Values 0, 2, 5, 6, and -1 matched value 1 exactly. Values 3 and 4 differed from value 1 and each other. With Outline=Shadow=0, values 1 and 3 matched. With Outline=0 and Shadow=4, they differed. These are libass-only checks. They do not verify box geometry against either VSFilter binary. Local fixtures, the check script, and full results are under .pi/style-investigation/. Run C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/python.exe .pi/style-investigation/check.py from the repository root to repeat them. These local artifacts are not tracked. The results file records commands and renderer logs. Recreate the fixture above if those artifacts are absent.

stylefield.name: alignment
stylefield.note:
Policy: ASS032 reports whole ASS v4+ Alignment integers outside 1 to 9. It does not compare frames or apply a fix. SSA uses a separate mapping. Status: source-verified for all three pinned renderers.
ASS values 1 to 9 select the usual numpad positions in all three sources. libass converts the integer into HALIGN|VALIGN at parse (ass.c:710-712; ass_utils.h:142-158). xy and VSFilterMod keep the integer. GetSubtitle first negates it to mark alignment as unset, parses tags, then applies abs before layout (xy RTS.cpp:2931,3001; VSFilterMod RTS.cpp:3944,4044). Layout uses value%3 for left, centre, or right, and value<=3 or value<=6 for bottom, middle, or top (xy RTS.cpp:1570-1575,3264-3269; VSFilterMod RTS.cpp:1915-1920,4381-4382). These different stored forms select the same ordinary positions.
Positive values above 9 are not rejected by these Style loaders. Horizontal position repeats every three values; vertical position stays at the top. For example, 10 selects top-left and 11 selects top-centre. This describes base layout only. xy has another margin adjustment switch with no case above the third row (RTS.cpp:4331-4336). Host margin settings can therefore add differences. ASS032 still treats these values as invalid.
Negative values except INT32_MIN become absolute values before layout. They can select the same base position as their positive counterpart. However, xy and VSFilterMod first negate the Style integer. A negative Style makes m_scrAlignment positive before tag parsing. Their an and a handlers require m_scrAlignment<0, so they ignore those tags (xy RTS.cpp:2301-2313; VSFilterMod RTS.cpp:2903-2913). Style value 0 also blocks those tags. libass uses parsed_tags separately and accepts a valid an override in both cases (ass_parse.c:584-604). Thus Style Alignment=-2 with {\an7} remains bottom-centre in VSFilter, but selects top-left in libass. Style Alignment=0 has horizontal bits 0 in libass. Its positioned anchor and line alignment have no matching case (ass_render.c:1943-1957,2324-2352). VSFilter combines a right-edge anchor with a centre fallback in different layout steps (xy RTS.cpp:1570-1572, 3264-3266,3332-3334). Do not assign one stable numpad meaning to value 0. INT32_MIN is a separate limit: libass chooses 2 to avoid signed overflow. VSFilter negation and abs cannot represent its positive value. A binary check is required; no portable result is claimed.
SSA: libass retains the legacy bitfield but changes 8 to 3 and 4 to 11 (ass.c:713-719). VSFilter loaders convert legacy bits to numpad values (xy STS.cpp:1545-1547; VSFilterMod STS.cpp:1908-1910). Common SSA positions agree. Legacy value 4 selects middle-right in all three base layouts. Legacy value 8 selects bottom-right in all three base layouts. Style-row conversion differs from the legacy a override, which has its own invalid-value handling. Do not apply the ASS 1-to-9 rule to SSA.
Runtime check: the libass build and fixture scope are recorded under BorderStyle. Alignment=-2 matched 2 without alignment tags. Alignment=10 matched 7. With Alignment=0, adding {\an7} changed the frames. With {\an7}, Alignment=-2 matched 2. All four comparisons met their expected results. No VSFilter runtime comparison or INT32_MIN check was done.

stylefield.name: marginl
stylefield.note: Both renderers store one integer with no post-processing. libass reduces modulo 2**32 (ass.c:292-321). GetInt uses swscanf, whose overflow behavior is undefined. A value inside the int32 range is equivalent.

stylefield.name: marginr
stylefield.note: Same integer rule as marginl.

stylefield.name: marginv
stylefield.note: Same integer rule as marginl.

stylefield.name: encoding
stylefield.note: Same integer rule as marginl. libass stores it in Encoding (ass_render.c:1110).

stylefield.name: tertiarycolour
stylefield.note: SSA only. libass reads the name as OutlineColour, then overwrites OutlineColour from BackColour (ass.c:694-697). xy and VSFilterMod copy BackColour into colours[2] (STS.cpp:1532,1885). The two paths reach the same slot by different routes. The byte-order question from primarycolour also applies.

stylefield.name: alphalevel
stylefield.note: SSA only. libass applies the alpha to the three front colours and forces the back alpha to 0x80 (ass.c:533-541,733-734). xy and VSFilterMod clamp the value to 0..0xff and set alpha[3] to 0x80 (STS.cpp:1533-1534, 1886-1891). Both clamp to one byte, so a value inside 0..255 is equivalent.

stylefield.name: justify
stylefield.note: Policy: retained, with no diagnostic. No Style-row conversion is modeled. Correction, source-verified: ass.c:615 belongs to ass_process_force_style, the host override API. It is not the ASS Style-row parser. process_style has no Justify field handler (ass.c:688-728). Adding a Justify column to a file therefore does not set ASS_Style.Justify in this pinned libass. The previous claim that the stored value had no reader was incorrect. init_render_context reads Style.Justify (ass_render.c:1152). align_lines uses it to set line justification independently of event alignment (ass_render.c:2305,2326-2350). Host values 1, 2, and 3 mean left, centre, and right. Value 0 follows alignment (ass_types.h:83-86). xy and VSFilterMod have no Justify field in their ASS Style loaders. This row does not treat the libass host API as an ASS file-format extension. Runtime check: changing the fixture Justify column from 0 to 3 produced identical libass frames. The build and fixture scope are under BorderStyle. The host override API was not run.
